rappel_detail.pull: Decide which side you are pulling from before the last climber leaves, and keep both strands clear of the clefts.
rappel_detail.notes: Topmost station reversing the South Face.
rappel_detail.anchor: 3 rap rings, backed by sling around tree/horn
hazards: Large clefts flank the line that look purpose-built to catch a rope - feed the rope down rather than throwing it
Trip reports repeatedly record the rope sticking on this descent and needing tugging to free
rappel_detail.station: A small step down from the summit leads to the notch where the easy version of pitch 4 ends, and the tree growing there is the top anchor. As of a 2021 inventory it carries three rap rings plus a quantity of slings and cord. About 25 m back down to the pitch-3 ledge.

hazards: A 60 m rope doubled comes up just slightly short of the tree at the top of pitch 2, so the last few metres are an unroped downscramble. An added pitch-3 anchor exists specifically to cut that exposure out on a 60 m
rappel_detail.station: The station on the pitch-3 ledge, where the first rappel lands. Currently an 8 mm cordelette doubled around the anchor with two quicklinks.

rappel_detail.pull: The tree sits back from the lip, so the rope saws across the flat top of the ledge and this pull is stiff. Pull from immediately beside the slung rock horn at the top of pitch 1 - moving any further out before pulling is what jams it.
hazards: The tree has taken most of the traffic on this peak for years and its long-term health is a stated concern - use the rock anchor beside it where it is in place
The lower rappels are lichen-covered and slippery when wet
rappel_detail.station: The ledge at the top of pitch 2: the anchor is the large, straight tree on the skier's-left side. Two trees here each carry a few slings, and by August 2024 a rock-based anchor had been added alongside them.

rappel_detail.anchor: several slings + 3 rap rings around a block
hazards: A slung block rather than fixed hardware: load it in line with the pull rather than shifting it

A second, partly hidden set of bolts sits off to the side of pitches 1 and 2 so descending parties do not have to share ground with climbers. It is a different line, and it needs a small swing climber's-right at the bottom to put your feet on the ground; continuing along the ramp there creates rope drag that makes the pull difficult
rappel_detail.station: Atop pitch 1, a block and horn carrying several slings and three rap rings - the same spot you pull the previous rope from. About 30 m returns you to exactly where you first roped up.

set.rappels: Most parties scramble the North Ridge to the true summit and descend the South Face rappel line: 4 single-rope rappels on a 60 m rope to Pineapple Pass. Alternatively, rappel Indentured Servant from its bolted anchors with a 60 m rope.
set.rappel_count_note: Four rappels on a single 60 m rope used doubled, each under 30 m, reversing the four pitches back to Pineapple Pass - this is what almost every party does and how the stations are spaced. Two 60 m ropes let you link them into fewer, longer rappels. One 60 m rappel in the sequence comes up just short of the next tree, leaving a short unroped downscramble, which an added pitch-3 anchor now avoids. A separate, partly hidden bolted line beside pitches 1 and 2 exists so that ascending and descending parties are not in the same place; it is a different set of anchors, not a variation. Below Pineapple Pass the east gully holds two more bolted chain stations for two further rappels on a 60 m - optional, and many parties scramble out instead; there is meaningful rockfall hazard in that gully. Do not scramble directly up to Pineapple Pass on the way in: that ground is the rappel route.
